reports.title: JD.com Completes Voluntary Public Takeover Offer of CECONOMY

desk.headline: Revenue back to growth, up 3.5% to RMB309.6bn, in line with estimates; adjusted EPS per ADS up 58% to RMB5.88 as food-delivery losses shrink; no guidance

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted per ADS, RMB; GAAP diluted RMB4.59 vs RMB3.39

results: Revenue returned to growth, up 3.5% to RMB309.6bn (about US$46.2bn); electronics and appliances slipped 0.7% while general merchandise grew 8.1%.
Profit improved sharply: operating income of RMB5.2bn versus a loss a year ago, and adjusted net income up 44% to RMB8.3bn.
Losses in New Businesses (mainly food delivery) narrowed to RMB9.6bn from RMB15.7bn, helped by a 26% cut in marketing spend.
JD Retail stayed steady with a 5.8% operating margin; JD Logistics revenue rose 16%.
Quarterly free cash flow was negative RMB23.9bn (seasonal working capital), though 12-month free cash flow rose to RMB18.8bn. The CECONOMY (MediaMarkt) takeover closed on 12 Nov.

guidance.summary: JD.com does not give financial guidance. Management only said near-term consumer demand remains uncertain.

points: Food-delivery losses fell by more than half from a year ago; the aim is a further big cut in spending on it in 2027.
Joybuy, the European online store, grew revenue 35% from the prior quarter with spending kept in check; CECONOMY synergies target supply chain, delivery and technology.
JD Retail gross margin hit a record 20.1%; the long-term goal is a high single-digit operating margin.
On trade-in subsidies, management said details await official announcements and timing effects cloud the electronics outlook.
AI tools such as the Dongdong shopping assistant and more warehouse automation were highlighted as efficiency drivers.

watch: Electronics sales and any new government trade-in subsidies.
First quarter of CECONOMY in the numbers and its effect on margins.
Further narrowing of food-delivery and New Businesses losses.
